extensions.question_or_target: What algorithm reliably detects that a set of sources supporting one claim all descend from a single origin - shared verbatim n-grams, shared factual errors, publication-date ordering, explicit backlinks - and what is its detection rate on a corpus with 10 planted citation cycles and 10 genuinely independent clusters?

answer.measured_candidate_algorithm: Build later-to-earlier derivation edges from distinctive exact n-gram overlap, shared catalogued factual errors, and explicit source backlinks. Publication time orients edges but never creates one. Keep an equal-time edge only when an explicit directed backlink is present. Select an edge only when it carries at least two evidence families. Collapse the cluster when every document reaches one covering root on that selected graph.

adversarial_holdout.ADV-COMPOSITE: independent (per-edge two-family; graph-wide union no longer fires)
adversarial_holdout.ADV-TIED: single-origin-cycle (explicit backlinks honored on equal timestamps)

answer.scope: Exact for the 22-cluster synthetic fixture including the two omitted-attack clusters. Field web corpora remain NOT-CHECKED.
